festivals: Mandalavilakku Utsavam (41 days, Malayalam month Vrishchikam, November-December) with Thacholikali
Annual Utsavam (8 days, Meenam, March-April): Theyyambadi Kurup, Nadu Valam Vekka, Pallivetta, Poorakkali, Poora Pattu

history.dynasty: Tradition credits 500 Aryan Nagariks (migrant Vaishya Brahmins) as founders; no dynasty documented
history.period: Traditionally ~1500 years old (verify - oral tradition only; the three shrines differ in age: Vishnu oldest, Bhagavathy ~1500 years, Shiva ~400 years)
history.summary: Lokanarkavu Temple at Memunda, about 5 km from Vadakara in Kozhikode district, is a Durga (Bhagavathy/Lokambika) temple and the family temple of the 500 Aryan Nagariks said to have migrated to Kerala - the Goddess is believed to have travelled with them in the form of a lady and is still conceived as their mother rather than only a Goddess. CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the CSV says Kozhikode, but the temple is at Memunda near Vadakara (Vatakara), not in Kozhikode city. Unique in Kerala for housing three deities in separate shrines with distinct rituals: Vishnu (oldest, north), Bhagavathy (main, worshipped as Saraswati in the morning, Lakshmi at noon, Bhadrakali in the evening), and Shiva (newest, centre). Protected as a heritage site by the Kerala Archaeology Department for its ancient murals. Closely associated with the Vadakkan Pattukal ballads - legendary martial hero Thacholi Othenan is said to have worshipped here daily - and with Kalaripayattu, whose practitioners seek the Goddess's blessings; Thacholikali is performed only here. Name derives from Lokamalayarkavu: lokam (world) + mala (mountain) + aaru (river) + kavu (grove).

name: Lokanarkavu Temple
town_description: Vadakara (Vatakara) is a coastal town in northern Kozhikode district, known as the home of the legendary martial hero Thacholi Othenan and the Vadakkan Pattukal ballads. It is a centre of Kalaripayattu tradition and has beaches, rivers and lush countryside. Vadakara town has its own railway station and is on the NH 66 corridor.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism, with Vaishnava and Shaiva shrines)

travel.railway: Vadakara railway station, about 5-6 km from the temple
travel.road: At Memunda, about 5 km from Vadakara town on the Kozhikode-Kannur route; local buses and autos available

visitor_information.best_time: Vrishchikam (November-December) for the 41-day Mandalavilakku, or Meenam (March-April) for the annual Utsavam
